Save Your Ass prep speech entirely absent — no prep-lowers-the-bill framing, no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip

Accepted a nonsensical square-footage answer ('it's $54 total... $54 square feet') without clarifying
top_strength: Outstanding objection handling on a demanding customer's four stipulations — she gave a concrete, confident answer on floor runners and wall padding, held the line politely but firmly twice on the no-booties/no-socks safety policy without ever getting defensive, committed to the unwrap-outside-and-leave-the-blankets request, and volunteered that Einstein uses background-checked W-2 employees rather than daily contractors, which directly answered his bad experience with a previous mover.
coaching_note: She earned the customer's trust and then never used it — she ran an 11-minute call that ended with zero pricing, zero clock, zero estimate and a promise to call back later. That callback is a second chance the customer may not answer, and it hands a hot, already-frustrated lead a gap to shop in. She had everything she needed to quote live. Specifically: PJ handed her Meet Your Mover and No Worries on a platter ('I had another company... the next time I got a totally different group and I was not happy' and 'everything is brand-new and I don't want it messed up'), and she answered both with policy detail instead of the branded differentiators. Next call: after the concerns are noted, transition with the agenda statement, finish the probe in one pass, and deliver pricing, the clock, the estimate and the Save Your Ass prep speech on the same call — never defer the quote to a callback when the customer is already on the line and ready to book.
phone_presence_notes: She used PJ's name constantly and naturally, repeatedly acknowledged his anxiety ('I understand,' 'Of course,' 'No worries, I'll put a note on your profile so they are prepared'), and moved him from combative about the date and stipulations to 'I'm very excited' and a warm 'thank you ma'am' close — though the affirmations lean on a narrow repeated set ('Yup,' 'Gotcha,' 'Okay').
audio_review_reason: The customer dominated the call and the transcript has significant garbling and overlap ('Yes I will wash out for those,' '$54 square feet,' '4050 blowing'); worth hearing the actual tone on the two consecutive refusals of the booties and socks request to confirm they landed as warm-but-firm rather than dismissive to a high-anxiety customer.
